regulation.title: Verordening (EU) 2016/679 betreffende de bescherming van natuurlijke personen in verband met de verwerking van persoonsgegevens en betreffende het vrije verkeer van die gegevens en tot intrekking van Richtlijn 95/46/EG (algemene verordening gegevensbescherming / AVG)

regulation.note: Companion/reference dataset, not a replacement for either uploaded source file. Both legal_text_nl.html and metadata.xml remain untouched at /mnt/user-data/uploads/.

SOURCE_TEXT_CURRENCY_FINDING.finding: UNLIKE the AI Act, no amendment relationship of any kind (amended_by, resource_legal_amended_by_resource_legal, plain or reified) was found for GDPR anywhere in this metadata file. This was verified explicitly, not just assumed from absence in one predicate list. GDPR's own consolidated-version history is limited to its 3 corrigenda (2016, 2018, 2021); there is no 'has_successor' consolidated version pointing to any later amendment (contrast with the AI Act, which had a 2026-07-27 post-Digital-Omnibus successor version).
SOURCE_TEXT_CURRENCY_FINDING.conclusion: legal_text_nl.html, despite being generated in December 2024, is NOT known to be outdated relative to GDPR's substantive articles as of this metadata snapshot -- there is nothing to be out of date relative to. It should already reflect all 3 corrigenda since all three predate the file's generation date.
SOURCE_TEXT_CURRENCY_FINDING.caveat: Two pending Commission proposals exist (see amendment_history) that would change this conclusion once/if enacted -- this is a 'currently accurate, watch this space' finding, not a permanent one.

amendments_to_own_text.note: Explicitly verified absent, both as plain triples and as reified OWL annotation axioms, in both directions. This is a genuine negative finding, not a gap in extraction.

items.note: Numbering (COM_2025_0837) is very close to the AI Act's own pending Digital Omnibus proposal (COM_2025_0836_FIN, found during the AI Act build). Strongly suggestive these are sibling proposals within the same Digital Omnibus simplification package, one per regulation -- NOT independently confirmed via document titles (none available in this metadata file), flagged as an inference.

explicit.name: Directive 95/46/EC (the previous Data Protection Directive)
explicit.location: Whole-instrument repeal, no specific article location in the metadata (consistent -- repealing an entire directive doesn't need one).
explicit.found_during: Second double-check pass -- the date was present in the metadata but omitted from the first two versions of this file.

implicit.name: Regulation (EC) 1882/2003 (comitology adaptation regulation)
implicit.location: Bijlage II, punt 18 (Annex II, point 18) of Regulation 1882/2003 specifically -- NOT the whole regulation.
implicit.found_during: Second double-check pass. This is a materially more precise fact than the first version of this file stated: GDPR's implicit repeal targets one specific annex entry of Regulation 1882/2003, not the instrument as a whole.

adopts.name: The original European Commission proposal for the GDPR
adopts.note: Confirms and dates the legislative_procedure field above (2012/0011(COD)) -- this is literally that proposal document. Found during the second double-check pass; omitted from the first two versions of this file.

phased_applicability.note: Matches GDPR's own well-known structure: signed/entered into force 20 days after publication (2016-05-24), but only became directly applicable two years later (2018-05-25, art. 99). The 2020-05-25 deadline corresponds to the first Commission evaluation report under art. 97.

case_law_and_litigation.methodology_note: GDPR's metadata uses TWO DIFFERENT location-code formats for different relationship types, discovered and handled separately: 'preliminary_question' and 'failure_of_obligation' use the same verbose {CODE|url} format as the AI Act; 'interpreted_by' (case-law) uses a completely different COMPACT format (e.g. 'A58P2LD') that required a dedicated parser, built and verified against the actual GDPR text before use (see decode_terminology_verification).

interpreted_by_case_law.unparsed_note: 'A06P1L1L3' does not fit the identified compact-format pattern; left undecoded rather than guessed.

cases_WITHOUT_article_level_detail.note: Found during the proactive double-check pass: these 14 cases have a direct 'interpreted_by' relationship to GDPR but no reified, article-level location annotation. The first version of this file's extraction only walked the reified annotations and would have silently omitted all 14 of these cases entirely -- caught by cross-checking direct triple counts (74) against reified distinct-case counts (60) and investigating the gap, rather than assuming they matched.

resulting_judgment.note: The single case-law record found under 'failure_stated_by' (cited 4 times, once per relevant provision) -- the judgment establishing failure of obligation.

citation_volume.correction_note: The first version of this section reported only 216 citing documents, taken from the reified 'work_cited_by_work' annotation records alone. This UNDERCOUNTED by a factor of roughly 10x: the reified annotations are only a subset (documents whose citation event carries extra metadata such as a date); the great majority of citations to GDPR exist only as plain, non-reified 'cited_by' triples. Found during the double-check pass by comparing direct triple counts (2265) against the reified-only count (216) -- the same kind of gap as the interpreted_by case-law omission above, now fixed the same way: by not trusting reified annotation completeness without checking the plain triples too.
citation_volume.note: Pure bibliographic noise for this project's purposes -- none of these citation records carry an article-level location code, so they indicate only that a document cites GDPR generally, not which provision. Full list of the 2265 distinct citing documents preserved below rather than discarded, per the no-information-loss requirement, but not individually decoded (that would mean identifying and describing 2265 separate documents, well beyond this dataset's purpose).

basis_for.note: Documents/instruments for which GDPR serves as a legal basis (e.g. implementing or delegated acts, adequacy decisions, other instruments citing GDPR as their enabling provision). Not part of the original build at all -- added during the double-check pass per the no-information-loss requirement. Not individually decoded or categorized in this pass; raw list preserved for anyone who needs to investigate further.

verified_directly_against_gdpr_text.PO/PT = punt (numbered): confirmed via Article 4's numbered definitions (point 2 = 'verwerking', checked directly)
verified_directly_against_gdpr_text.PTA/L+letter = punt (lettered): confirmed via Article 58(2)(d) and Article 6(1)(f), both checked directly against real text
verified_directly_against_gdpr_text.SCT = Afdeling: confirmed, GDPR uses 'Afdeling 1' etc. as chapter subdivisions, 'Sectie' appears 0 times
verified_directly_against_gdpr_text.ALN/L+digit = alinea: confirmed, 'eerste alinea, punt f)' matches exactly
verified_directly_against_gdpr_text.AN = Bijlage: N/A for GDPR -- confirmed GDPR has zero annexes ('BIJLAGE' appears 0 times), and no AN codes appear in any extracted location, consistent.

NOT_independently_verified_best_inferenc.FR (verbose format): Assumed 'zin' (sentence), inferred from a sentence-count match in one example (Article 38(6) has exactly 2 sentences, matching 'FR 2'). Not confirmed against an official code table.
NOT_independently_verified_best_inferenc.SNT (compact format): Assumed 'zin' (sentence) for the same reason as FR, but SNT and FR are DIFFERENT codes in two different encoding systems within the same file -- their both plausibly meaning 'sentence' is not proof they are formally equivalent or that either translation is officially correct.
NOT_independently_verified_best_inferenc.PTI: Occurs once, decoded identically to PTA ('punt'). Could not determine why GDPR's/AI Act's data uses a separate code; the practical decoded output is very likely correct regardless (Article 23(1) point (i) is confirmed to exist), but the distinction between PTA and PTI remains unexplained.

decode_terminology_verification.recommendation: Treat FR/SNT-based 'sentence'-level precision as directionally reliable but not to be quoted as an authoritative citation without further confirmation; the article/paragraph/point level (the vast majority of all decoded locations) is independently verified against real text and can be relied on.

double_check_log_round_2.purpose: This user explicitly requested a further double-check pass after round 1 (which had already fixed the 14-missing-cases and 2049-missing-citations gaps). This log documents what round 2 found that round 1 missed.

found_and_fixed.issue: The 'repeals', 'implicitly_repeals', and 'adopts' relationships were noted in amendment_history but without their dates or, for implicitly_repeals, its precise location. All three actually have dates in the metadata (2018-05-25, 2018-05-25, 2016-04-27 respectively), and implicitly_repeals has a specific location: Bijlage II, punt 18 of Regulation 1882/2003, not the whole regulation.
found_and_fixed.found_via: Checking which of the 4971 annotation records had a non-null 'date' field at all (only 3 did) -- a check not run in round 1.

found_and_fixed.issue: Several document identifiers in the citation_volume and basis_for raw lists were stored URL-encoded (e.g. '62024CO0090%2801%29' instead of the readable '62024CO0090(01)', '12012M%2FTXT' instead of '12012M/TXT').
found_and_fixed.found_via: Explicitly scanning all target identifiers for '%' characters -- 16 such entries found, confined to work_cited_by_work (45 records) and resource_legal_basis_for_resource_legal (3 records); confirmed the four carefully-decoded categories (interpreted_by, preliminary_question, failure_of_obligation, corrections) were NOT affected.

checked_and_confirmed_clean: All axiom node IDs are distinct (4971 records, 4971 distinct node IDs) -- no duplicate-counting.
Compact-format entity prefixes are exhaustively only 'A' (Artikel) and 'C' (considerans) across all 175 interpreted_by records -- no unhandled third prefix.
None of the three carefully-decoded case-law categories contain any percent-encoded identifiers needing cleanup.

The single unparsed compact-format code ('A06P1L1L3') remains genuinely unresolved after a second attempt at manual interpretation -- left flagged rather than guessed, since no interpretation could be verified against the actual text.
still_not_independently_verified: FR and SNT sentence-level codes (unchanged from round 1's assessment)
PTI vs PTA distinction (unchanged from round 1's assessment)

The is_about / EuroVoc subject-matter classification data (14 direct triples) exists in the source but was not extracted into this file at all -- a lower-priority classification-metadata category, not an amendment/citation/case-law fact, flagged here for completeness rather than silently ignored.
